The '''spatial curvature parameter''', often denoted by $k$, models the spatial part of the [[spacetime]] curvature in the relativistic model of our [[Universe]]. It appears in various equations in [[cosmology]].<ref>{{#cite:Q2580}}</ref>

== Significance ==

Assuming [[the Cosmological Principle]], the [[Universe]] must be maximally symmetric, hence:

{| class="wikitable center"
|-
! Spatial curvature parameter ($k$)
! Shape of Universe
! [[Spatial curvature radius]] ($R_c$)
! Geometric model of space
|-
| $k=0$
| '''Spatially flat'''
| $R_c=\infty$
| 3D [[Euclidean space]]
|-
| $k<0$
| '''Open'''
| $R_c>0$
| 3-hyperboloid
|-
| $k>0$
| '''Closed'''
| $R_c>0$
| 3-sphere with finite volume
|}

<ref>{{#cite:Q2580}}</ref>
